scenes.title: Four merchants, one engine
scenes.caption: Four merchants. Same codebase. Bealls — off-price apparel. Bealls Florida — regional variant. Home Centric — content-mode, no checkout. And Sleep Country — high-stakes mattress retail. Same Aisles repo, same engine, four genuinely different commerce contexts.

scenes.title: Watch the engine compose
scenes.caption: Cold load. The shopper hits the page, and the engine starts composing. The dev panel reads the signals as they arrive — hunter at sixty-five percent — and an AI agent is selecting blocks, ordering sections, and writing copy in real time. Five to ten seconds. Not pre-baked. Composed for this shopper.

scenes.title: Hunter layout, with provenance
scenes.caption: Layout settles. Every block tagged. Category-header, product-grid — each one labeled with the engine that produced it and the persona it was composed for. This isn't a template. It's a live composition. The dev panel shows hunter at sixty-five percent, forty-seven point gap, one rule fired, and exactly which blocks the engine chose.

scenes.title: Same URL, researcher composition
scenes.caption: Same URL. Same shopper context. But this time the engine read researcher — seventy-one percent confidence, fifty-five point gap. Different blocks: editorial-header, expanded copy, comparison-friendly grid. Every block tagged with researcher provenance. The engine adapts — same code path, different composition, no developer in the loop.

scenes.title: The engine, observable
scenes.caption: And this is what engineers see. The Observe dashboard — every signal a shopper emits, the inference state at each tick, the persona probabilities. This is production telemetry. Not a smoke test, not a debug page bolted on. It runs in the same pipeline as the engine.

scenes.title: When intent shifts, the engine sees it
scenes.caption: Same dashboard, the moment intent changes. Hunter to researcher — the engine flagged the shift and tells you why. Three rules fired, weights visible, every signal accountable. No black box. If a persona moves, you see exactly which rule moved it.

scenes.title: Grounded in real data
scenes.caption: Where do the persona priors come from? For Sleep Country: eleven thousand real shopper sessions, seven weeks of BigQuery data, anonymized before it left the warehouse. Hashed IDs. Hour-bucketed timestamps. No personal data. Enough signal to calibrate against. No risk to anyone.

scenes.title: Six of ten transferred
scenes.caption: Then we ran our existing inference rules against that ground truth. Six of ten testable rules transferred from off-price apparel to sleep retail unchanged. Three pointed the wrong direction. A Facebook click in apparel is browsing. In sleep retail, it's paid-social purchase intent. So we corrected three rules — surgical, per-brand. One ADR. Same engine.

scenes.title: Real shoppers, replayed
scenes.caption: Twelve replay fixtures, each one a real anonymized journey from the BigQuery data. Pick one, hit replay. The events fire through the same signal pipeline production uses. The persona vector updates live. The layout regenerates. Every demo, reproducible. Every claim, traceable to a real session.

scenes.title: Merchant control — Rules
scenes.caption: And this is what merchants see. The Aisles admin panel — embedded inside the BigCommerce dashboard. Pin a product. Exclude another. Boost a category. Schedule a seasonal override. Per persona, per category, time-windowed. Merchants don't write code. They curate.

scenes.title: Merchant control — Analytics
scenes.caption: Same panel, the analytics tab. Cost. Cache hit rate. Persona breakdown. Daily generation cost. Merchants own engine health, not just shopper UX. If something starts costing more or hitting cache less, they see it without filing a ticket.

scenes.title: Merchant control — Preview
scenes.caption: And the preview tab. Render any persona, any category, any time. Merchants see what shoppers will see — before they ship a rule change. The same composition pipeline as production, with their pending edits applied. Closed loop, no surprise launches.

scenes.title: Calibrated, not heuristic
scenes.caption: Aisles isn't a product. It's a calibrated engine. Observable for engineers. Controllable for merchants. Grounded in shopper data, not vendor intuition. Same engine, four merchants today. Bring your data, we calibrate the engine.
